walkthroughs.h2: Driving big loads from a chip
walkthroughs.body_html: A microcontroller pin only supplies about 20 mA. To drive a motor we use a transistor as a switch: a small base current allows a large collector current. A flyback diode protects the transistor from voltage spikes when the motor turns off.

Designers sketch a flow chart before coding. Diamonds are decisions (Is it dark?), rectangles are actions (Turn LED on), and arrows show the path. The chart maps directly onto if-then-else code blocks.
Setting a PWM pin to 50% duty cycle makes an LED appear half-bright by switching it on and off very quickly. PWM also controls motor speed and servo positions without wasting power as heat.
